newsitem.title: USA: IMF says Turkey needs strong stabilization plan.
newsitem.headline: IMF says Turkey needs strong stabilization plan.

text.p: Turkey needs to take bold steps to stabilise its fragile economy and reduce raging inflation, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said in a strongly-worded statement on Tuesday.
"Directors highlighted the adverse effects of high inflation on the sustainability of output growth," the IMF executive board said in a summary of its annual review of the Turkish economy.

"They strongly urged (the government) to embark on a bold and comprehensive programme of stabilisation policies and structural reforms to reduce inflation and set the economy on a sustainable growth path," the summary said.

The IMF, which completed its review of the Turkish economy last month, said fiscal consolidation would have to be the linchpin of any stabilisation effort, including a reform of the country's deficit-ridden social security system as well as an "acceleration in the privatisation process."
Urgent steps should be taken to eliminate the various legal and other obstacles to privatisation and to foreign investment, particularly in the energy sector, it said.
The IMF also said Turkey's ailing banking system needed major reforms.

"Directors expressed concern about weaknesses in the banking sector, especially the low earnings, capitalisation, and liquidity of the state banks, which required immediate attention," the statement said.

Turkey's new left-right coalition government has vowed to jumpstart stalled privatisations and battle inflation, currently just under 80 percent. The government is targeting end-year inflation of between 80 and 85 percent.
